source: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 14 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 14
knowledgePattern: Turn a fractional-part integral into one recurrence multiplier
solution:
On each interval j/n≤x<(j+1)/n, where j=0,…,n−1, the fractional part is {nx}=nx−j. The graph of |4{nx}−2| forms a V of width 1/n, with height 2 at either end and zero at its midpoint.

The two triangles in one V have total area 1/n. There are n such pieces in [0,1], so the integral is 1. Values at the isolated endpoints do not change the area.

Thus an+1=an and every term equals a1=1/2. The partial sum of the first N terms is N/2, which grows without bound. The series diverges to +∞. Answer F.

hints.title: Start with n = 1
hints.body: For 0≤x<1, the fractional part of x is just x. Sketch |4x−2| on this interval and find the area using triangles.
hints.recap: The integral of a nonnegative graph is its area.
hints.pitfall: The fractional part resets at an integer; a single endpoint does not change the area.

recall.reminder: The integral of a nonnegative graph is its area.

hints.title: See what n changes
hints.body: As x runs from 0 to 1, nx passes through n unit intervals. The fractional part starts again in each one, making compressed copies of your first graph.
hints.recap: Horizontal compression changes widths, not heights.
hints.pitfall: Include the width of a copy when finding its area.
hints.pause: Find the area of one copy, then the area of all n copies.

recall.reminder: Horizontal compression changes widths, not heights.

hints.title: Return to the sequence
hints.body: Put your integral value into the rule for the sequence. Write the first few terms, then see what happens when you keep adding them.
hints.recap: An infinite sum is finite only if its partial sums approach a fixed number.
hints.pitfall: Do not use the geometric-sum formula before checking its common ratio.
hints.pause: Decide whether the partial sums settle at a finite value.

recall.reminder: An infinite sum is finite only if its partial sums approach a fixed number.
